release_identity.cache_identity: BuildName/CacheBust/ConfigStamp/UIStamp are derived from metadata.lua; version bump creates a fresh release cache namespace

runtime_architecture.movement_ownership: RE4MovementCoordinator + RE4TravelResolver + one RE4TweenRuntime active tween + event-driven RE4TransitionGuard; map-induced relocation cancels stale tween state before bounded route re-resolution
runtime_architecture.combat_ownership: RE4CombatTargetLock + RE4CombatPulse + one scheduler-managed RunService.Stepped FastAttack connection
runtime_architecture.bring_ownership: owner-scoped RE4BringService with network-ownership gate and deterministic restore
runtime_architecture.character_lifecycle: RE4CharacterLifecycle invalidates travel/target/bring/combat state before character rebind

core_recovery.reference: Cr4Hub_base(1).lua used selectively for post-update movement/bring/hit contracts; duplicate Cr4 attack loops were intentionally not ported
movement: player tween baseline remains 200 studs/s; dynamic far/near phase model from 2.0.6 is unchanged
Sky Lower and Sky Upper are explicit transition-sensitive movement zones instead of both collapsing to World
the lower Sky endpoint is restored to its Sky3Exit semantic role; exit portal use requires SkyUpper source and SkyLower destination
FastTravel filters transition-sensitive portal candidates by source/destination zone before route-cost comparison
follower divergence caused by an external map teleport cancels the single active tween immediately and syncs the movement anchor to the actual player position
wrong-layer external transitions create a bounded session-local hazard and mark the responsible portal/target route unsafe
route re-resolution is event-driven and capped; learned hazards use two geometric detour waypoints rather than random delay, portal spam, or infinite retry
destination changes across movement zones preempt the old request instead of mutating a route calculated for another layer
detour segments abort on target revision so a moving destination cannot leave a stale waypoint route active
movement OFF/owner cancel/preemption/respawn continue to cancel the active tween and follower state through the existing lifecycle
noclip: BodyClip reused and zeroed with 1e9 MaxForce
movement lifecycle destroys BodyClip and releases collision source
bring: network ownership required before client CFrame correction
owned BodyVelocity hold uses 1e9 MaxForce and zero velocity
original collision/humanoid movement restored on release
Bring toggle OFF stops all holds immediately
dead/corrected group member releases its hold immediately
combat: primary target is always included in BladeHits
hit part resolves Head then limbs then root fallback
COMBAT_REMOTE_THREAD true requires native SendHitsToServer bridge; false uses RegisterHit; unknown flag sends neither
bridge discovery refreshes on character respawn
ui: Choose Attack Speed dropdown and obsolete speed-mode config/globals removed
Fast Attack remains a single ON/OFF control feeding one attack scheduler

offline_regression.live_verification: Roblox runtime is unavailable in this container. Exact cloud trigger bounds and server teleport behavior cannot be certified offline; 2.0.7 therefore uses topology semantics plus runtime-observed relocation instead of claiming a fixed trigger CFrame.

movement_update_2_0_6.scope: player movement/tween only; BringMob, mob movement, combat, attack and UI are unchanged

dynamic.implementation: two sequential tween phases; speed is never mutated on a running Tween
dynamic.guard_effect: cancel current near tween through the single runtime, suppress near boost for the rest of the session, and reissue the current route once at fallback speed

movement_update_2_0_6.live_validation_note: 350 cannot be certified from this offline container. It is treated as a short-range candidate and automatically disabled if observable movement instability occurs. 200 remains the only assumed stable baseline.

movement_update_2_0_7.scope: player movement/FastTravel topology only; BringMob, mob movement, combat, Fast Attack and UI are unchanged
root_cause: 2.0.6 classified all normal Sky layers as World, so route ownership had no layer identity after a map-triggered teleport
the -4607/874/-1667 entrance was stored as generic Sky2 even though the reference flow identifies the endpoint as Sky3Exit
the follower resynced block after a large root jump but did not invalidate the tween that was still interpolating toward the stale pre-transition route
solution: event-driven external relocation cancellation and bounded route re-resolution
session-local hazard learning and geometric detour for a repeated wrong-layer segment
movement_update_2_0_7.runtime_note: Exact trigger geometry is learned only when the game actually relocates the player; no single cloud coordinate is hardcoded into movement logic.
